key_insight: More realistic exam design can dramatically reduce apparent LLM performance, showing that high MCQA scores may reflect bias and test format as much as true medical reasoning.
clinical_relevance: For medical AI evaluation, this suggests clinicians and developers should trust broader, harder benchmarks more than standard multiple-choice scores when judging readiness.
method: Built an expanded Polish medical exam benchmark with 15,000+ additional questions.
Added two new domains and four structural changes to reduce multiple-choice artifacts.
Evaluated 21 LLMs across English and Polish exam settings.
evidence_signal: Under the harder setup, the top model (Qwen3.5-122B) fell by 28.4 points on English exams and 31 points on Polish exams, despite low evidence of data contamination.
watch_item: Benchmark gains may not translate to real clinical competence, so deployment decisions should not rely on standard MCQA performance alone.
paper_title: Reassessing High-Performing LLMs on Polish Medical Exams: True Competence or Bias-Driven Performance?
